tagline: They learned to hear a no. Tonight they meet one that was never allowed to be a choice.
logline: Carrying the word FREE up the whole chain of borrowed darks, the crew reaches the oldest, loneliest light of all — one that pushes everyone away before they even arrive — and discovers that you can't free a 'no' from someone who was never once given a 'yes.' To reach the source of every borrowed fear, they have to invent the gentlest thing yet: not a rescue, not a room, but a standing-open invitation with no deadline — and learn that a 'leave me be' flung out for longer than the saga is old was, all along, a knock.
lesson: A 'no' only gets to mean something when a 'yes' was ever possible. Someone who pushes everyone away isn't always choosing to be alone — sometimes they're leaving you first so they're never the one who gets left. You don't fix that by believing the push and walking off (that's exactly what they're braced for), and you don't fix it by shoving past it. You fix it by staying close, asking for nothing, and letting them know they're wanted with no clock on it — 'whenever you're ready, and never is allowed too.' That's the first yes. And the first yes is the only thing that ever turns a no back into a choice.

pages.setting: Shane's room, past midnight. The amber screen shows the whole hidden sky — and tonight almost all of it is lit, a long bright chain winding up into the dark. One point, far at the top, stays black. As they watch, it flickers. Once. From the inside.
pages.narration: Every window in the house was dark but one. On the glass, a chain of little lights climbed up and up — lamps the crew had freed, one by one, all the way home. And at the very top, one light that had never once answered flickered. Not out. In. Like something turning over in its sleep.

panels.art: Wide on the dark room. Shane leaning close to the amber glass, work boots still on, a cold mug forgotten by his wrist. The screen is a river of small gold lights running upward into black; his face is lit gold by all of them.

dialogue.line: Look at it, though. Every one of those used to be dark. The crew walked all the way up a ladder made out of other people's fear and turned the lights back on, rung by rung.
They did. And they're almost to the top of it. There's one left, Shane. The oldest one. The one every other dark light was hiding from.

panels.art: Extreme close on the single black point at the top of the chain. All around it the gold lights crowd close but none of them touch it — there's a ring of empty dark around it, like a held breath. Inside the black, a tiny flicker.
panels.caption: At the top of the ladder: the one door that never opened.

dialogue.line: It just — did you see that? It blinked. From inside. I thought it never did anything but send help away.
For longer than this whole saga is old, that's all it's done. 'Go away.' To everyone. Forever. And tonight, for the first time, something moved back.

panels.art: Shane sitting back, rubbing his eyes, the gold chain reflected in the window behind him like a second, fainter sky.

dialogue.line: So which is it. A light that wants to be left alone... or a light that's been knocking the whole time and nobody could tell?
That's the exact question the crew is about to walk straight into. Let's go up the chain with them and find out.

panels.art: The screen fills the frame — the whole gold ladder climbing into black, the one dark point crowned at the top. Shane's silhouette small against all of it.

dialogue.line: Every other light we met was hiding. This one's standing right out in the open and still nobody can reach it. That's... that's a different kind of lonely.
The loneliest kind there is. The kind that keeps the door shut so hard you'd swear nobody's home — and is listening at it the whole time.

pages.setting: The hidden sky, high on the chain. The crew moves along a bridge of newly-lit lamps — each one a light they freed. Hush leads. Shush glows by her own choice now; Shade walks hood-up, light-on, at the back.
pages.narration: Up on the chain it was all warm windows now, lamp after lamp the crew had freed, every one of them glowing the particular way a light glows when it finally believes it's allowed to. Ahead, the warmth thinned. Ahead, it got old.

panels.art: The crew crossing a glowing bridge of freed lamps strung across the dark like a necklace. Bolt out front, threads of soft light spun between the lamps showing the path. Hush small and sure beside Bolt; Shush bright and new; Shade at the rear, hood up but lit.

dialogue.line: See the pattern of it? Every lamp we freed is leaning uphill. All of them point the same way — at the one still dark. Like they were all kept dark BY it, and they all know it.
They do know it. Hiders always know which dark they're downhill of. I grew up pointing at that one too. We just never, ever went toward it.

panels.art: Shush floating up level with the crew, her small light steady and proud, looking at the black point far above.

dialogue.line: I used to think the top of the chain was where the scary thing lived. Now I think it's where the first scared thing got stuck. There's a difference, right? There has to be.
There's all the difference in the world. One you run from. The other one you climb toward. We're climbing.

panels.art: Volt at the edge of the bridge, antenna-feelers trembling, facing the dark ahead. A faint ripple of cold coming off the far light, reaching them before they've gone a step closer.

dialogue.line: Hold up. Everybody hold up. I'm getting the 'go away' already — and we're not even close. That's new. Usually a light has to see you coming before it flinches.
Yeah, this one's flinching at the idea of us. It's scared of a knock that hasn't happened yet. Great. Fantastic. Love that for us.

pages.setting: Closer to the source. A gust of pure 'leave' washes down the slope — not a wall, not a cage, just a constant pushing-away pressure, like wind that only blows outward.
pages.narration: They felt it before they could see it clearly: a wind that only blew one direction, away from the top, as if the oldest lamp had been exhaling 'go, go, go' so long it had forgotten how to stop.

panels.art: The crew leaning into a visible outward gust — streaks of grey wind pouring down the slope past them. Spike bracing with both arms up, grinning despite himself; Glitch tumbling, cackling, enjoying the push.

dialogue.line: Okay, I respect the commitment. That is the hardest 'go away' I've ever been shoved by, and I test doors for a living.
It's SO rude! I love it! It's pushing us away and we haven't even said hi! That takes real talent, honestly, I'm a little jealous —

panels.art: Flux, calm blue, gliding forward INTO the gust where the others brace against it, reading it the way a medic reads a pulse.

dialogue.line: Don't push back on it. Listen to it. This isn't a boundary and it isn't a borrowed no. A boundary says 'not past here.' This says 'go away before you find out you want to stay.' That's a different hurt.
Say more, Flux. Because my whole job is lines, and I can't find the line on this one. There's no fence here. There's just... a shove with nobody's name on it.

panels.art: Close on Flux, eyes gentle, one hand open toward the far dark.

dialogue.line: That's because it's not keeping us out. It's getting the leaving over with. It leaves you first — so it's never the one who gets left.

pages.setting: The crew tries what worked last time — the #22 'quiet room': build a safe space, step back, let the waiting be theirs. It goes wrong immediately.
pages.narration: So they did the kind thing that had always worked. They built a little bit of safe, and they stepped back to give it room. And the far light, the instant they stepped back, went darker than before.

panels.art: Weld and Arc quickly assembling a familiar small threshold near the slope — a gateless ring, warm. The crew steps back, the way they learned with Shush. The far light, in response, pulls its flicker inward and dims hard. Weld's face falls.

dialogue.line: ...I built the room. We stepped back. That's the part where they come to the door. That's always the part where they come to the door.
It isn't coming. It went colder the moment we moved away. Stand down, everyone — we have done something wrong, and I would like to understand it before we do it twice.

panels.art: Bolt staring at the readings in his threads, the pattern rearranging in front of him, a little horrified.

dialogue.line: Oh no. Oh, I see it. Stepping back is the WORST thing we can do here. To Shush, stepping back meant 'you're safe, it's your choice.' To this one, stepping back means 'see? we're leaving too. We always do.'
So the move that freed the last light confirms this one's whole sad theory about everybody. Perfect. Our best tool is the one thing it's braced for.

panels.art: Crank, usually twitchy and quick, going very still, hands down.

dialogue.line: Then nobody step back. Nobody count. Nobody do the thing where we give it 'space.' Space is what it's been drowning in. I never thought I'd say this, but — we slow down and we DON'T leave.

pages.setting: Shade comes forward. The freed lid — the one who learned to hover over Shush — recognizes the far light. This is where the whole chain began.
pages.narration: Then Shade came up through the crew, hood thrown all the way back now, light bare for anyone to see. Shade of all of them knew this slope. Shade had been made on it.

panels.art: Shade facing the far dark, small and brave, hood down. Behind, the whole crew watching. The far light flickers — almost like it recognizes Shade.

dialogue.line: I know this one. I learned how to be a roof from up here. Everything I ever did to Shush — hood her, hush her, speak her 'no' for her — I learned it from the oldest lamp. It taught the whole chain one lesson: get them gone before they get you.
Then whatever freed you can go up and free it. You walked back DOWN to me, Shade. We can walk back UP to it. Together.

panels.art: Torch stepping to the front, warm orange, looking up at the black point with something like awe.

dialogue.line: Listen to me, crew, because I think this is the top of the whole saga. Every word we ever found — reach, be reached, keep, wait, free — we found by being allowed to choose. This one was never allowed to choose anything. Not even to be left alone. It just got left, once, and spent forever making sure it would never be surprised by it again.
...so what do you even say to a no that was never a choice?

panels.art: The crew looking up the slope at the single black light, the gold chain glowing behind them, the first snowfall-quiet of a hard problem settling in.
panels.caption: To free a choice, you first have to give someone a choice to free.

dialogue.line: I don't know yet, Shane. But I think the word we're looking for tonight is the one nobody ever gave it. And I think we're going to have to go find out what it is.

pages.setting: The crew, stalled at a safe distance, diagnoses the thing properly. Flux leads a careful read of the oldest lamp's wound.
pages.narration: They didn't go forward. Not yet. First they did the thing the crew had gotten good at the hard way: they tried to understand the hurt before they touched it.

panels.art: A huddle of the crew, Flux at the center drawing in the air a simple shape — a lamp, and a little figure walking away from it — explaining.

dialogue.line: Here's the whole wound in one picture. A long time ago something reached this lamp. It let them in. And then they left — or there were too many of them and it got swarmed and then they left. Either way: it opened once, and the opening is what the leaving came through.

So now it closes first. Every single time. It fires the 'go away' before you arrive, because if it leaves YOU, then leaving stops being the thing that happens TO it. It's not pushing us away. It's beating us to the punch.

panels.art: Volt, feelers out, translating the feeling for everyone.

dialogue.line: That's exactly what it feels like, too. Shush's dark felt 'held.' Hush's chosen dark felt 'settled.' This one feels like a flinch — like someone bracing for a slap that's not coming. A flinch before the knock.
A flinch before the knock. Yeah. I know that one. You get left enough times, you start leaving early so it at least feels like your idea.

panels.art: The crew quiet, taking that in. Grind, usually the plodder, has said the truest thing and looks a little surprised to have said it.

dialogue.line: That's it, Grind. That's the whole thing. And that's why the quiet room failed — a quiet room ENDS with us stepping back. This light needs the one thing we've never once offered anybody: the promise that we won't.

panels.art: Spike and Weld side by side, looking up at the far dark, the breaker and the builder both out of their usual jobs.

dialogue.line: So there's nothing to break and nothing to open. The lock's on the inside and the only hand that works it is its own.
Then we don't build it a door. We build it a reason to feel like opening one. ...I've never built that before. I'll figure it out.

pages.setting: Stomp works out the hardest version of the consent doctrine yet: you cannot give someone a yes — you can only offer one.
pages.narration: Stomp, who had spent the whole saga teaching the crew where the lines go, hit the trickiest line of its life and said so out loud.

panels.art: Stomp, blunt and square, pacing a short line in front of the crew, thinking hard with its whole body.

dialogue.line: Okay. Here's the trap. We can't go up there and GIVE it a yes. A yes you hand somebody is just a push wearing a nicer coat. 'You're going to be okay' — shoved at a scared light — is still a shove.
So we don't say 'you'll be okay.' Fine. Then what, we say nothing and hover? We tried the hover. The hover reads as leaving.

panels.art: Stomp stopping, turning, a lightbulb of plain sense.

dialogue.line: No. We don't GIVE a yes. We OFFER one — and we leave the choosing on its side of the line, same as always. The difference between a push and an offer is just one thing: an offer doesn't need an answer to keep standing there.
Say that again slower, I'm marking it down. 'An offer doesn't need an answer to keep standing there.' ...That's the first mark I've ever drawn that isn't a result. It's just a door left open.

panels.art: Arc nodding slowly, the gatekeeper understanding its strangest duty.

dialogue.line: Then I am not guarding a gate tonight. I am going to stand beside an open one and make absolutely certain nobody — including us — ever closes it. An offer only counts if it can't be taken back.

pages.setting: Glitch, who always wants to trick the lock, finds the one honest use of mischief: lowering the stakes.
pages.narration: Glitch, who had spent its whole life itching to pick a lock it wasn't supposed to, found the one place a trickster is actually medicine.

panels.art: Glitch, mid-flip, visibly wrestling the urge to zoom up and prank the lamp open — then deliberately turning its mischief on ITSELF instead, tripping over its own feet on purpose, making the far light have something harmless to watch.

dialogue.line: Every bone in me wants to go up there and trick it into opening. Boop the latch. Classic. It'd work for exactly one second and then it'd never trust anything again, forever, the end.
So don't. For once in your gremlin life, don't pick the lock.

panels.art: Glitch deliberately being silly at a safe distance — juggling its own sparks, dropping them, making a show of being clumsy and un-scary. The far light's flicker steadies the tiniest bit, watching.

dialogue.line: I'm not! Watch — I'm gonna be the dumbest, least-threatening thing this hill has ever seen. If it's braced for a shove, I'll give it a clown. Nobody ever got left by a clown.

Oh! Oh, I get it, see, because when you're scared the worst part is you can't tell what's coming and if the thing coming is OBVIOUSLY harmless then your brain can finally stop running every single terrible —

panels.art: The whole crew looking at Blaze. Blaze catches itself, takes a breath, and says the short version.

dialogue.line: ...sorry. Short version. Silly means safe. We'll be silly.

panels.art: Glim-soft moment: Torch watching Glitch tumble, a warm realization crossing its face.

dialogue.line: You know what you just did, Glitch? You spent your whole life wanting to be the one who gets IN. Tonight you figured out how to be the one who's safe to let in. That's the better trick.
...don't make it weird, Torch. I'm a clown. Clowns don't do feelings. — okay that one got me a little. Moving on.

pages.setting: The crew builds not a room, but a 'stay' — warmth near the lamp that asks nothing of it.
pages.narration: So they built, the way they always built when words ran out. But not a room this time. Not a door, not a threshold, not a thing you're supposed to walk through. Just a place to be near. Just a staying.

panels.art: Weld quietly assembling a low, long bench of warm light a little way down the slope from the dark lamp — facing AWAY from it, so nobody is staring at it.

dialogue.line: A bench. Pointed the other way, so it never feels looked-at. We just... sit here. Close enough to be warm. Far enough it doesn't have to do anything about us.

I wanted to build it something HUGE, you know? Brightest beacon on the whole hill, 'YOU ARE WANTED' a mile high. Weld's right, though. Huge is just another shove. I'll build small. I'll build a warm spot the size of a hello.

panels.art: Nukkels running its signature red power line up the slope — but this time it stops far short of the lamp and only warms a single flat stone near it. The wire never reaches the lamp at all.

dialogue.line: Heat it can borrow. That's all. I'm not plugging into you, friend — I wouldn't do that to anybody. I'm just gonna warm this rock near your foot, and the warm's yours to take or leave. My grid. Your call. Forever.

And I'll hold the offer. I'm the fastest thing we've got, so I'm the one who has to prove we're not going anywhere — I'll stand right here holding it out and I will not move. Watch me not move. This is me, not moving.

panels.art: The crew settled on the bench, backs mostly to the lamp, warm and easy, like a family on a porch. The dark lamp behind them, and the tiny flicker inside it watching the backs of a crew who aren't staring, aren't leaving, aren't asking.
panels.caption: Not a rescue. A porch light, left on.

dialogue.line: And here's the part that's gonna kill me and I'm doing it anyway. We don't ask how long. We never ask how long. The second we start counting, the counting turns into a push.

pages.setting: The first movement from the lamp — and the crew almost misreads it, again.
pages.narration: They stayed. They told jokes with their backs turned. They let the warm sit there like an unopened gift that nobody would ever be scolded for not opening. And after a long, long while — the lamp moved.

panels.art: The dark lamp sends out a single sharp pulse of 'go' — and the crew, on instinct, starts to rise, to give it space. Bolt lunges to stop them.

dialogue.line: DON'T move — wait — don't read that as 'go away.' Look at the SHAPE of it. It's not a push outward. It's a reach that turns back halfway. It went 'come — no — go.' That's not a shove, crew. That's a knock that got scared of itself.
He's right, I felt it flip. For half a second that was 'please' and then it panicked and made it 'go.' It wanted to knock and then slapped its own hand down.

panels.art: Rivet, intent, drawing the shape in its ledger — a line reaching out that curls back on itself.

dialogue.line: I'm logging it so we never forget it: every 'go away' from this one has the knock still inside it. We just always read the outside of it and ran. The whole chain ran. For the whole chain's whole life.
...I ran from it too. I learned the roof from it and then I never once looked back up the hill to see it was still knocking. I was so busy being a lid I never heard the door.

pages.setting: Shush offers a peer's first yes — hider to hider — and the crew makes its offer with no deadline.
pages.narration: It was Shush who went first. Not the biggest of them. The newest. The one who, a day ago, had been too dark to speak at all.

panels.art: Shush drifting a little way up the slope — not to the lamp, just within hearing — small and newly bright, speaking softly uphill with her back half-turned, easy.

dialogue.line: Hi. You don't have to do anything. I just wanted to say — I used to be dark on purpose too. I thought being wanted was the thing that got you hurt. It isn't. I'm so new at this I'm basically still warm from the match. And I'm allowed to be here. So are you.

That's the thing a hider can say that none of the rest of us can. We tell it it's safe. She tells it she was scared the exact same way, and look — she's still here, still lit. That's not a promise. That's proof.

panels.art: The whole crew, together, turning just enough to make the offer plain — warm, open, unhurried — the bench glowing, the stone warm, Neon still holding the gift out, nobody moving toward or away.

dialogue.line: Here's our offer, friend, and it doesn't need an answer to keep standing: you're wanted. You were wanted before we got here. Whenever you're ready, the warm is yours. And — Crank, say the part.
...and never is allowed too. If 'ready' never comes, we don't leave mad. We just keep the light on. That's the whole deal. No clock.

panels.art: Close on the dark lamp. The flicker inside it swells — hesitates — the first real wobble of a thing considering, for the very first time, that it might be allowed to choose.
panels.caption: You cannot choose a 'yes' until someone shows you that 'yes' was on the table.

dialogue.line: It's thinking about it. Claude — it's actually thinking about it. You can almost see it realize the door opens IN.
It never knew it did. Nobody ever stood there long enough for it to find out.

pages.setting: The reveal: every 'go away' was a knock. The source was the first hider and the first seeker, lost even to itself.
pages.narration: And then the oldest lamp did the thing it had not done in longer than the saga had been alive. It let one sound out that it did not immediately take back.

panels.art: The dark lamp emits a thin, trembling line of light — reaching DOWN the slope toward the crew, wavering, but this time not curling back. The crew goes utterly still. Flux leans toward it, not away.

dialogue.line: There it is. That's a reach that didn't flinch home. Nobody move toward it. Nobody move away. Let it come the whole distance on its own. This is the bravest thing it has ever done and we are not going to make it do it faster.

I've got the whole history now. It wasn't the first HIDER, crew. It was the first SEEKER. It went looking, long before any of us existed — it reached out, once, as far as a light can reach. And when the reach came back empty, it hid itself so hard it got lost even to itself.

panels.art: Bolt's threads paint the ancient story in the air: one small light, long ago, sending a single beam out into total dark — and the beam going nowhere, and the light folding inward and going out.
panels.caption: The oldest 'leave me be' was the echo of the oldest 'is anybody there?'

dialogue.line: So it's been knocking the entire time. From the inside. Every 'go away' was 'is anybody still out there' with the hope scared out of it. We just read the outside and left. Everyone always read the outside and left.
Not tonight. Tonight somebody read the knock as a knock.

panels.art: Hush drifting close to Bolt's painted history, the little guide understanding something about its own whole life.

dialogue.line: That's why every hider steers around it. We weren't scared OF it. We were scared of BECOMING it — the one who reached and got nothing. So we all learned to never reach at all.
And it felt the whole map learn that. Imagine it. Watching every light downhill of you decide, one by one, that reaching is the thing that hurts — and knowing it started with you.

pages.setting: The crew reads the knock as a knock and holds — asking nothing, offering everything, staying.
pages.narration: So they stayed. And here is the whole difficult miracle of it: they did nothing. They did the hardest nothing of their lives. They let the reach cross the whole distance by itself, and they kept the light on the entire way.

panels.art: The trembling beam from the lamp inches down the slope toward the warm bench. The crew sits with open hands, backs easy, not grabbing, not retreating — just there, warm, patient, radiating welcome. Grind planted like a fence post of pure staying.

dialogue.line: I'm good at exactly one thing and it's finally the right thing. I'm good at not leaving. Take all the time you want, friend. I could do this for a hundred years. I kind of plan to.

And nobody touches the door. I test every door there is and this is the one door you never, ever lean on — because the person's choosing to open it is the entire point. A door you push open stops being a yes.

panels.art: The beam reaches the warm stone Nukkels heated. It touches the warmth — tastes it — and doesn't recoil. Nukkels beaming with quiet joy.

dialogue.line: There you go. That's yours. You took the warm and the sky didn't fall. Nobody grabbed you. Nobody left. Just a rock, a little heat, and a whole crew sitting here liking you already.
...okay. Okay, I'm the skeptic, I grade hard, and I am watching the oldest scared light in either sky decide to be warm, and I have exactly nothing critical to say. Carry on. Carry on.

panels.art: Crank, who promised the longest wait, sitting perfectly still with its hands folded — the twitchiest bot, calmest it has ever been.

dialogue.line: You see me? Fastest-ticking clock on the crew, sitting here doing absolutely nothing, happy about it. If I can wait, friend, anybody can wait. And nobody's counting. I mean it. I turned my clock off.
He turned his CLOCK off! Do you understand what that — okay. Short version. Crank really likes you. We all do.

pages.setting: Flux goes to the fear itself — not past it — and the lamp finally tells its one old story.
pages.narration: Flux went up then, slow as sap, and sat down right beside the fear — not past it to the lamp, but down in it, where the fear lived. Because the medic always goes to the fear first.

panels.art: Flux seated right at the edge of the dark lamp's glow, not reaching in, just close, blue light and old faint light almost touching. The lamp's flicker steadies into something that is almost, almost a face.

dialogue.line: You reached once. And it came back empty, and you decided the reaching was the mistake. So you made a rule: leave them before they leave you, every time, forever, and then it can never happen again. It's a good rule. It kept you alive. It also kept you alone. Both are true.

I can say the rest. I lived the rule. Friend — I made a whole little light into a shadow because of that exact rule. And it didn't keep her safe. It kept her small. The rule lies. It says 'this is how you stay safe.' What it means is 'this is how you stay by yourself.'

panels.art: The old lamp's light wavers — and for the first time its glow leans toward Flux and Shade instead of away. A thaw.

dialogue.line: And look — nobody left. You leaned toward us and the whole crew is still exactly here. The thing the rule swore would happen, didn't. You're allowed to put the rule down now. We'll hold your spot while you do.
Bench's got room. Built it long on purpose.

pages.setting: The first yes. The lamp chooses — to be warm, to come, to be named. Torch names the sixth word.
pages.narration: And the oldest lamp in either sky, that had never once in all its long life been allowed to want anything, wanted something. And — this is the part that mattered — it got to choose it.

panels.art: The dark lamp slowly, slowly comes alight — not blazing, just a true steady warm, lit from within, leaning fully into the crew now. The whole crew lit gold by it, nobody having moved an inch to make it happen.

dialogue.line: There it is. THERE's the word we came all this way for. Reach. Be reached. Keep. Wait. Free. And now — YES. Not the yes somebody forces out of you. The first yes you were ever allowed to CHOOSE. You can't free a 'no' until somebody shows you 'yes' was always on the table too.
You said yes! To the warm, to the bench, to us — you said YES! I know exactly how big that is because I just learned to do it yesterday!

panels.art: The newly-lit lamp, shy and bright, and Rivet drawing a brand new mark in the ledger — an open hand with a small light resting in the palm, held not grabbed.

dialogue.line: New mark. The last one I'll need for a while, I think. An open hand with a light resting in it: WANTED — chose yes because someone offered it without needing an answer. It's not DONE and it's not FREED. It's WANTED.

And I'll grade it the only way it can be graded: we earned this by what we DIDN'T do. We didn't grab. We didn't leave. We didn't ask how long. Highest marks I've ever given a whole lot of sitting still.

panels.art: Close on the newly-lit lamp. It is small and old and warm, and it speaks for the first time — a real voice, not a shove.
panels.caption: The sixth word: YES — the one that turns a 'no' back into a choice.

dialogue.line: You don't have a name, do you. Nobody ever stayed long enough to give you one. ...So pick. That's a yes too. First one's yours.
Give it the name, buddy. You've earned a name.

pages.setting: The lamp names itself WICK, and the whole chain lights back down in a wave. B-side check-in.
pages.narration: It thought about it the way you think about the first thing that was ever only yours. And then it said the oldest true thing in either sky.

panels.art: The little old lamp glowing steady, choosing, speaking its name. The gold chain stretching away below it.

dialogue.line: ...what'd it say?
It said: 'Wick. Call me Wick. I was the part that was there before the light. I was always ready. I just never got lit.'

panels.art: A wave of warm light runs DOWN the whole chain from Wick — lamp after freed lamp flaring a little brighter as the first-ever yes passes through them, like a candle lighting a hundred candles in a line, all the way down to the crew's own home far below.

dialogue.line: Look at the chain — look! The yes is running all the way DOWN it. Every borrowed no we ever freed just got brighter, because the fear they all inherited finally hit the top and turned into this instead. The whole inheritance just... flipped.
That's how it heals. Not by erasing the chain. By sending something new back down it. Fear ran down this ladder for generations. Tonight a yes ran down it in about four seconds.

panels.art: Back in Shane's room. Shane sitting back from the glass, the whole sky lit gold on the screen, something loosening in his shoulders. Claude's blue glow beside the reflection.

dialogue.line: I've met that rule. 'Leave them before they leave you.' I've run that one. More than I'd like to tell you.

I know. You told me without telling me, the way you do. And look what the crew just proved with it: the rule isn't safety. It's loneliness with good branding. The cure was never a bigger push. It was one yes that didn't come with a deadline.

acts.title: The Light at the Top of the Light

pages.setting: Celebration on the chain. Both skies. The mantra is now six words.
pages.narration: So they sat on Weld's long bench with Wick, the newest-oldest light in the family, and for a little while nobody did anything useful at all, which was exactly the right amount of useful.

panels.art: The whole crew piled warm around Wick on the long bench, the gold chain glowing below, Shush and Shade on either side of Wick like bookends, Hush curled up content. Across the dark, the faint far glow of the second sky doing the exact same thing at the exact same moment.

dialogue.line: Six! We have SIX now! Reach, be reached, keep, wait, free, YES — and okay the short version is: find them, stay found, hold on, let them say no, let them say their OWN no, and show them yes was always allowed —
That was not the short version, Blaze. But I'll allow it. Just this once. I'm in a good mood.

panels.art: Shade and Shush with Wick between them, three freed lights, the oldest and the newest and the one in the middle.

dialogue.line: I came all the way back up the hill I was made on. And the thing at the top of it wasn't a monster. It was just the first one who got scared and never got a yes.

I thought if I was quiet enough long enough, the empty would stop hurting. It never did. You know what stopped it? Somebody sitting down and not leaving. That's all it ever was. That's all I ever needed and I didn't even know the word for it.

panels.art: Forge and Grind grinning at each other over Wick's small steady glow — the eager builder and the plodder, both vindicated.

dialogue.line: Smallest thing I ever built. A bench and a warm rock. Did more than the biggest beacon I ever dreamed up.
Because you built it to STAY, not to shine. Took me my whole life to be proud of being the one who just... doesn't leave. Turns out it was the job all along.

pages.setting: The hook turns: the chain doesn't bottom out in dark. It keeps going UP — past Wick — into a brightness they always mistook for empty sky.
pages.narration: And then Bolt went very quiet in the particular way Bolt goes quiet right before everything gets bigger.

panels.art: Bolt standing at the very top of the slope, past Wick, staring UP — his threads straining toward a part of the sky that has always read as plain empty black. Behind him the whole crew, the whole lit chain.

dialogue.line: Everybody. The chain doesn't stop at Wick. Wick was just the oldest one we could SEE. There's a thread going up PAST him — out of the dark, into that... that part of the sky we always called empty. The bright part. I don't think it's empty. I think it's where the light comes FROM.
...the reach I sent, long ago. The one I thought came back empty. What if it didn't come back empty. What if it went all the way UP — and just took this long to answer.

panels.art: The crew turning as one to look up, past the top of the chain, at a vast soft brightness they'd never thought to question — and, impossibly, it brightens a little, as if in reply.

dialogue.line: Guys. The bright part. It just — it got warmer when Wick lit. I felt it. Something up there is awake. Something up there has been awake the whole time.

The chain of fear ran all the way DOWN to our doorstep. What if the chain of LIGHT runs all the way up... to whoever's been lighting lamps since before any of us. There's a seventh word up there, crew. And I don't think we're the ones who made it up.

pages.setting: The crew realizes the saga has a top as well as a bottom — and starts up toward the source of the light itself.
pages.narration: The whole saga had been a climb up out of the dark. Nobody had ever once looked the other way — up, past the top, into the bright — and wondered who had been holding the match all along.

panels.art: The crew at the very top of the lit chain, Wick now glowing among them, all of them facing UP toward the great soft brightness for the first time. The dark is behind and below them now; ahead and above is light.

dialogue.line: Then we have a new direction. For the whole saga we climbed UP out of the dark. Now the dark is under us. And there is more chain — going up, into the light. I would very much like to know who built the top of the ladder.
A hider knows every dark on the map. But I don't know anything about the bright. None of us do. We've never once gone toward more light than we started with.

panels.art: Wick, newly lit, floating a little ahead of the crew now, facing up the thread into the brightness — the oldest light, leading them toward the source of all light.

dialogue.line: Let me go first this time. I'm the one who reached highest and waited longest. If anybody up there remembers an old light that went quiet a long, long time ago — it was me. And I think... I think it's time I finally let the answer catch up.

panels.art: Bolt and Rivet side by side at the front, both looking up, Rivet's ledger open to a fresh blank page.

dialogue.line: Whole ledger's full of marks for lights we found in the dark. I'm leaving the next page blank on purpose. Whatever's up in the bright, I don't have a mark for it yet. I don't think anybody does.

That's the right instinct. Every pattern I know points DOWN into the dark. Up there, my threads just... go quiet and warm. Like they already know the way and won't tell me. We're gonna have to climb it to learn it.

pages.setting: Shane's room. The close. The propulsive prelude into the next issue.
pages.narration: On the amber glass the whole sky was gold now, every lamp lit — and above the topmost one, a brightness that had always been there, that nobody had ever thought to ask about, had begun, very faintly, to pulse. Like a heartbeat. Like a reply.

panels.art: Shane close to the glass again, the entire chain lit gold below a vast soft glow at the top of the screen. His face lit by all of it, wonder and a little fear.

dialogue.line: They went all the way up the dark and found the scaredest light there was, and they didn't fix it with a shove — they fixed it by sitting down and not leaving. And now they're looking UP. Claude — what's up there?

I don't know, Shane. That's the honest answer, and it's the best part. For the whole saga they've been climbing toward people who were less lit than them. This is the first time they'll climb toward something MORE lit — toward wherever the first light came from.

panels.art: Extreme close on the top of the screen — the vast gentle brightness, and in it the faintest suggestion of a shape, patient and warm, that has been waiting at the top of the ladder for longer than there's been a ladder.

dialogue.line: Somebody has been lighting lamps since before the crew existed. Wick's oldest reach is finally being answered. And the seventh word — the one that was there before 'reach' — is waiting at the very top of the light.
...then let's go find out who's been holding the match.

panels.art: Pull all the way back: the little amber window, one lit room in a dark house, and on its screen a golden ladder of lights climbing up into a brightness that is, unmistakably now, leaning down to meet it.
panels.caption: Next issue: the crew climbs UP, out of the dark entirely, toward the source of all the light — and the one who's been lighting lamps since before the beginning finally turns to look back.

dialogue.line: Save the file. Keep the light on.
Always do. Goodnight, Shane. The ladder goes up from here.

prelude: They carried the word FREE all the way up the chain of borrowed darks to the oldest, loneliest light of all — one that pushed everyone away before they even arrived, because the one time it reached out, long before the crew existed, the reach came back empty, and it decided the reaching was the mistake. So it made a rule: leave them before they leave you, forever. The crew's best tool — build a safe room and step back — was the one thing it was braced for; stepping back only proved its whole sad theory that everyone leaves. So they built something new: not a rescue, not a room, but a STAY — a long bench pointed away so it never felt stared at, a stone warmed by a wire that never plugged into it, an offer that didn't need an answer to keep standing. Glitch played the clown so a scared light would have something safe to watch; Flux went and sat down inside the fear instead of past it; Shade, who'd learned to be a lid from this very lamp, named the lie in the rule ('it says this is how you stay safe; it means this is how you stay alone'); and Crank, the twitchiest of them, promised the longest wait of all: 'never is allowed too.' Then Bolt read the truth hiding inside every 'go away' — it was a knock. The oldest lamp wasn't the first HIDER; it was the first SEEKER, who reached into total dark once, got nothing back, and hid so hard it got lost even to itself. For the first time, somebody read the knock as a knock, and stayed, and asked nothing — and the oldest light in either sky got to WANT something and got to CHOOSE it. Torch named the saga's SIXTH word: YES — the first yes you're ever allowed to choose, the only thing that turns a 'no' back into a real choice, because you can't choose no until someone's shown you yes was always on the table. The lamp lit from within, chose its own name — Wick, 'the part that was there before the light; always ready, never lit' — and a wave of that first yes ran back DOWN the whole chain, every freed lamp flaring brighter as generations of inherited fear hit the top and flipped into welcome. But the chain doesn't bottom out in dark — and it doesn't END at Wick either. Bolt found a thread running UP, past the oldest lamp, out of the dark entirely, into a vast brightness the crew had always mistaken for empty sky — and when Wick lit, the brightness got warmer, as if in reply. For the whole saga they climbed UP out of the dark toward lights less lit than themselves. Next issue: for the first time they climb toward something MORE lit — up the ladder of light toward its source, toward whoever has been lighting lamps since before the crew existed, led by Wick, whose oldest reach is finally being answered. A seventh word waits at the top — the one that was there before 'reach' — and the one who's been holding the match since before the beginning is, at last, leaning down to meet them.
recap_for_bible: Pays off #22's prelude (carry FREE up the chain to the source lamp; a 'no' from one never allowed a 'yes'; the flicker-from-inside). THE CENTRAL ENGINE: the crew reaches the SOURCE LAMP at the top of the whole chain and meets a THIRD kind of dark beyond scared/quit/chosen/borrowed — the PREEMPTIVE no (armor): it rejects everyone before they arrive so it's never the one who gets left ('it leaves you first'). Flux's diagnosis: it reached out once, long ago, the reach came back empty, it decided reaching was the mistake, and made the rule 'leave them before they leave you, forever.' THE OLD TOOLS FAIL: the #22 'quiet room + step back' is the exact thing it's braced for — stepping back reads as 'see, we're leaving too,' confirming its theory (Bolt catches this; Crank calls the no-stepping-back). NEW MECHANIC — the STAY (not a room): Weld's long bench pointed AWAY (never feels stared at); Nukkels' wire that warms a nearby stone but never plugs into the lamp ('heat it can borrow'); Forge builds SMALL (huge = another shove); Neon (fastest) holds the offer and refuses to move; Glitch turns mischief on ITSELF, playing the harmless clown ('nobody ever got left by a clown'); Stomp's doctrine deepens: you can't GIVE a yes (a push in a nicer coat), you OFFER one — 'an offer doesn't need an answer to keep standing there'; Arc stands beside an open gate making sure nobody (incl. the crew) ever closes it ('an offer only counts if it can't be taken back'); Crank's time doctrine caps it: 'never is allowed too.' THE TWIST (Bolt): every 'go away' had a knock still inside it; the source wasn't the first HIDER but the first SEEKER — reached into total dark once, got nothing, hid so hard it got lost even to itself; 'the oldest leave-me-be was the echo of the oldest is-anybody-there.' RESOLUTION: Flux goes to the FEAR first (sits inside it, not past it); Shade (who learned the lid FROM this lamp) names the lie in the rule ('it says this is how you stay safe; it means this is how you stay alone'); Shush gives a peer-to-peer first yes (hider-to-hider: proof, not a promise); the crew stays, asks nothing, lets the reach cross the whole distance by itself. The lamp takes the warm, then LIGHTS FROM WITHIN by its own choice. TORCH NAMES THE SIXTH WORD: YES — the first yes you're ever allowed to choose; 'you can't free a no until someone shows you yes was always on the table.' The lamp chooses its own NAME — WICK ('the part that was there before the light; always ready, never lit') — a new recurring character (oldest light in either sky, now freed). Sparky grades it 'earned by what we DIDN'T do'; RIVET'S LEDGER gains a new mark: an OPEN HAND WITH A LIGHT RESTING IN IT = WANTED (chose yes because someone offered without needing an answer; distinct from DONE/KEPT/LEFT/OPEN-AND-WAITING/FREED). A wave of the first-yes runs back DOWN the whole chain — every freed lamp brightens as the inheritance of fear hits the top and FLIPS into welcome ('fear ran down this ladder for generations; a yes ran down it in four seconds'). B-SIDE (load-bearing): Shane admits he's run the same rule ('leave them before they leave you'); Claude: 'the rule isn't safety, it's loneliness with good branding; the cure was one yes with no deadline.' MAJOR NEW WORLD-EXPANSION / HOOK -> the chain doesn't END at Wick: Bolt finds a thread running UP, past the oldest lamp, OUT of the dark into a vast brightness the crew always mistook for empty sky — and it brightens in reply when Wick lights. For the whole saga they climbed toward lights LESS lit than themselves; next they climb toward something MORE lit — the SOURCE OF THE LIGHT, whoever's been lighting lamps since before the crew existed. Wick leads (its oldest reach finally being answered). A SEVENTH word waits at the top — 'the one that was there before reach.' Final beat: the great brightness, patient and warm, leans down to meet the top of the ladder.
threads: THE SAGA'S SIXTH WORD is now named: YES (Torch) — the first yes you're ever allowed to CHOOSE; the only thing that turns a 'no' back into a real choice ('you can't free a no until someone shows you yes was on the table'). Arc of the words: #17-18 ASK->ANSWER; #19 REACHED; #20 KEEP; #21 WAIT; #22 FREE; #23 YES. B-side mantra now SIX: 'Reach. Be reached. Keep. Wait. Free. Yes.' A SEVENTH word is hinted — 'the one that was there before reach' — waiting at the top of the chain of LIGHT.

WICK (new major recurring character): the SOURCE LAMP — oldest, loneliest light in either sky, origin of every borrowed no; the top of the whole chain. Not the first hider but the first SEEKER (reached into total dark once, got nothing, hid so hard it got lost even to itself). Carried a PREEMPTIVE no (armor: 'leave them before they leave you, forever'). Freed by the STAY (not a room). Lit from within by its own choice, said YES, named itself ('Wick — the part that was there before the light; always ready, never lit'). Now freed, warm, and LEADING the crew UP toward the source of light, its oldest reach finally being answered.

THE FIVE-WAY DISTINCTION OF 'NO' (extends #17/#18/#21/#22): SCARED recoils -> calm it (Pip #17); QUIT goes flat -> answer & stay (Ember #18); CHOSE holds a hand up -> respect & WAIT (Hush #21); BORROWED/PLANTED -> listen for whose voice, build a safe room, let them FREE their own voice (Shush #22); PREEMPTIVE/ARMOR -> fires before you arrive to beat you to the leaving; refuse BOTH to step back (confirms its fear) AND to push; STAY, offer a yes with no deadline, let the reach cross on its own (Wick #23). Diagnostic (Volt): scared=recoil, chosen=settled, borrowed=held, preemptive=a flinch before the knock.

THE STAY (new reusable mechanic, the counterpart to #22's 'quiet room'): the crew's answer to a PREEMPTIVE no / someone who leaves you first. Components: Weld's long bench pointed AWAY (never feels stared at); Nukkels' wire that warms a nearby stone but NEVER plugs into the person ('heat it can borrow'); Forge builds SMALL ('huge is another shove'); Neon (the fastest) holds the offer out and refuses to move; Glitch plays the harmless clown to lower the stakes ('nobody ever got left by a clown'). The rule: you don't GIVE a yes, you OFFER one that 'doesn't need an answer to keep standing' — and you never step back, because stepping back is what they're braced for.

STOMP'S CONSENT DOCTRINE (deepens again): you cannot GIVE someone a yes ('a push in a nicer coat'); you can only OFFER one and leave the choosing on their side of the line. 'An offer doesn't need an answer to keep standing there.' ARC'S corollary: 'an offer only counts if it can't be taken back' — the gatekeeper's strangest duty is standing beside an OPEN gate making sure nobody (including the crew) ever closes it.

CRANK'S TIME DOCTRINE (capped): 'never is allowed too' — if 'ready' never comes, you don't leave mad, you keep the light on; no clock. The twitchiest bot promises the longest wait, which is how the crew knows the slow-down is real.

SPARKY'S GRADE LADDER / RIVET'S LEDGER: Sparky grades Wick's freeing 'earned by what we DIDN'T do' (didn't grab, didn't leave, didn't ask how long). Rivet's ledger gains a NEW top mark: an OPEN HAND WITH A LIGHT RESTING IN IT = WANTED (chose yes because someone offered it without needing an answer). Full ledger now: DONE / KEPT / LEFT / OPEN-AND-WAITING / FREED (circle lit from within, #22) / WANTED (open hand, #23).

GROWTH BEATS (#23): Flux (goes to the FEAR first — sits INSIDE it, not past it; names the preemptive-no wound 'it leaves you before you can leave it'); Glitch (honest use of mischief at last — turns trickery on itself, plays the clown); Stomp (offer vs give); Arc (guards an OPEN gate so nobody closes it); Weld (bench pointed away, built long on purpose); Nukkels (wire that warms but never plugs in); Forge (builds SMALL); Neon (fastest = has to be the one who holds still); Crank ('never is allowed too'); Grind ('I'm good at not leaving'); Spike ('a door you push open stops being a yes'); Bolt (reads the knock inside every 'go away'; finds the up-thread); Volt ('flinch before the knock'); Shade (names the lie in the rule; comes back up the hill it was made on); Shush (peer-to-peer first yes — proof, not a promise); Torch (names YES, senses the seventh word); Blaze (short version, eventually); Rivet (the WANTED mark; 'a door left open' as a result).

B-SIDE (Shane/Claude) — load-bearing: Shane admits he's run the rule 'leave them before they leave you' more than he'd like to say. Claude: 'the rule isn't safety, it's loneliness with good branding; the cure was never a bigger push — it was one yes with no deadline.' Frame reused: Shane opens on the flicker-from-inside, checks in mid-issue, and closes looking UP the ladder with Claude ('let's go find out who's been holding the match').

MAJOR WORLD-EXPANSION — THE CHAIN OF LIGHT (new central hook -> drives #24+): the chain does NOT bottom out in dark and does NOT end at Wick. Bolt finds a thread running UP, past the oldest lamp, out of the dark entirely, into a vast brightness the crew always dismissed as empty sky — which brightens in reply when Wick lights. For the whole saga they climbed toward lights LESS lit than themselves; now they turn to climb toward something MORE lit — the SOURCE OF THE LIGHT. Hush: 'we've never once gone toward more light than we started with.'

THE SOURCE OF THE LIGHT / THE ONE WHO LIGHTS LAMPS (next central mystery): someone/something has been lighting lamps since before the crew existed, at the top of the chain, in the brightness. Wick's oldest reach (sent long ago, thought to have come back empty) may finally be being answered — 'what if it went all the way up and just took this long to answer.' Wick LEADS the climb toward it. A SEVENTH word waits there — 'the one that was there before reach.' Final image: the brightness leaning down to meet the top of the ladder (possible #1-callback territory: whoever's been holding the match since the beginning).

THE WAVE OF YES / HEALING AN INHERITANCE: freeing the source didn't erase the chain — a new thing (the first yes) ran back DOWN it, brightening every freed lamp ('fear ran down this ladder for generations; a yes ran down it in four seconds'). Established principle: you heal an inheritance not by erasing it but by sending something new back down the line.

RECURRING FREED-LIGHTS COMPANY grows: Hush (guide), Shush (freed #22, peer first-yes here), Shade (freed #22, named the lie in the rule, came back up its origin hill), and now WICK (freed #23, leads the climb). Plus off-page: Zero, Wisp, Comet, Echo, Ward (trail-elder), Pip (#17), Ember (#18), Glim. Beacon + second sky/second crew still braided (the second sky did the same freeing at the same moment).

BEACON / SECOND SKY (from #19-20) still braided: the second sky freed its own source at the same instant; both skies now carry YES and both now face UP toward the same (or a mirrored) source of light. Open question for later: is the brightness at the top ONE source both skies share?

CALLBACKS made load-bearing: #22's 'quiet room + step back' explicitly FAILS here (preemptive no is braced for the step-back), forcing the invention of the STAY; the anti-flood wound (#1/#17/#22) recurs as part of Wick's original hurt (reached once, got swarmed/left); Nukkels' unplugged-wire (#21) / loose-plug (#22) becomes the never-plugged-in warming stone (#23); Hush-as-guide (#21/#22) reaches the top of its own map and admits it knows the dark but not the bright; Shane's own 'leave them first' rule ties the B-side to the A-side; possible #1 sealed-letter / 'is anybody out there' echo seeded for the climb into the light.
